_readme: The declaration behind scripts/check-w10a-sdk-capability-premise.mjs. See E8-F007.
`surfaceMarkers` are the literal strings a human READ in the resolved package on the
date below. They are quoted, not inferred: the defect this guard closes is a sentence
about a dependency that nobody re-read for a year.
`stalePatterns` are stored as regex SOURCE strings so this file does not match the
pattern it declares (`not\s+fully\s+lockable` as literal text contains backslash-s,
not whitespace).
This declaration asserts a CAPABILITY IN AN ARTIFACT. It asserts nothing about whether
the operator's E2B tier honours a network body at runtime. That was unmeasured when this
file was written; the separate probe unit has since run (workflow run 34085130892,
2026-09-07) and MEASURED THAT IT DOES NOT FOR ONE SHAPE -- a denyOut CIDR list with no
allowOut. The tier accepts, validates, stores and
echoes the deny set back verbatim, and routes the denied traffic anyway. Finding E8-F008.
NARROWED 2026-09-09 (W10B-B): the default-deny-plus-allowOut construction E2B documents as
the fine-grained control is UNMEASURED; an arm for it is built (W10B runbook section 13).
That arm was DISPATCHED TWICE on 2026-09-09 (runs 34328502574 and 34328780645) and returned
UNRUN -- arm-was-never-created -- both times: Sandbox.create failed to place the body with a
500 'Failed to place sandbox ... please retry' while the sibling arms placed seconds apart on
the same template. So the documented shape REPRODUCIBLY FAILS TO PLACE at this tier (cause
unknown; a 500-with-retry-hint is not a validation refusal, and it is not transient because it
reproduced with successful siblings) and enforcement for it is STILL UNMEASURED. UNRUN IS NOT
INERT. Unmeasured is not 'probably works' -- DE-08 stays not-delivered.
Neither reading changes this file's job: the CAPABILITY claim is what is pinned here, it
still stands, and the surfaceMarkers below are unaffected. Do not read this file as
'egress is locked', and do not read the new result as 'the old premise was right' --
the old premise asserted the API did not EXIST, which is still false.

surfaceMarkers.why: the egress option type exists at all: allowOut / denyOut / rules / allowPublicTraffic
SandboxOpts — i.e. Sandbox.create's own options — carries it
SandboxInfo carries it back, so an applied configuration is READABLE (the read-back that makes a tolerant or self-hosted 200 detectable)
a RUNNING sandbox's egress configuration can be replaced
the runtime actually serialises the option rather than declaring a type nothing sends
and puts the result in the POST /sandboxes body
the update endpoint is real, not a type-only stub
getInfo maps the server's response back, which is what a read-back verification would consume

stalePatterns.why: The sentence family that actually occurred, in six tracked files, for a year: 'Managed-E2B egress is not fully lockable' (REFUTED as a capability claim — E8-F007). It is a NEGATIVE CAPABILITY CLAIM about a dependency, and the installed dependency contradicts it (surfaceMarkers above). Quoting it stays legal — the record has to be able to quote what it corrects — but only with a correctionMarker within contextWindowLines. This pattern covers the sentence, NOT the idea: a rewording evades it, and saying so is cheaper than letting a reader believe the class is covered.
